items.title: gpu-unlock: a Linux kernel module that roughly doubles FP16/BF16 tensor throughput on RTX 30-series cards (3090: 75 to 135 TFLOPS in PyTorch)
items.summary: gpu-unlock (github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock, created Oct 18, about 4.3K stars, no license yet) is a Linux kernel module that lifts the halved FP16/BF16-into-FP32 tensor issue rate on GA102/103/104/106 consumer Ampere cards. KBlueleaf measured a 3090 going from 75 to 135 TFLOPS in PyTorch at 360W, and the README reports a 3090 Ti BF16 GEMM going from 87.5 to 157.4 TFLOPS, user reports of +25 to 81%, LLM prefill gains of 14 to 36%, unchanged decode and INT8, and bit-identical outputs. It is unofficial and Linux-only; KBlueleaf also reports a similar unlock on a 2080 Ti.

doubt.source: Open-source repo with reproducible GEMM numbers and multiple user reports in the README.

reception.summary: Repliers are excited and mostly ask about other cards (3060 Ti, 5070 Ti, A6000, DGX Spark) and Windows support; a few note decode stays bandwidth-bound and ask for prefill numbers, which the README provides. Quotes are mostly reposts of the result.

items.title: Independent RTX 5090 test of vLLM's Humming kernels: 4-bit Qwen3.8-27B goes from 56.9 to 71.6 tok/s, about even with Marlin
items.summary: An outside test of the Humming quantized-kernel library (released by vLLM and Ant Group on Oct 21) on a consumer RTX 5090: with NVFP4 Qwen3.8-27B in vLLM, switching to Humming took a single request from 56.9 to 71.6 tokens/s, 26% over the kernel vLLM picks by default on that card. Against the older Marlin 4-bit kernel it was a tie (75.8 vs 77.1 tok/s), so the gain on this card is mainly over vLLM's default choice.

doubt.source: First-hand single-request benchmark on one card.
